Build the release's isopycnal table: conditions on density surfaces, every CTD down cast

Source: R/isopycnal.R
build_isopycnal.Rd

Calls calcofi4r::cc_isopycnal() — the one implementation of the isopycnal rule, never a copy of it — over every calcofi_ctd-cast cast in the connection, batch cruises at a time (the down cast of an occupation is chosen within its cruise, so batching changes nothing), and writes the result as one table in the release's conventions: one row per cast x surface x type, the type named by calcofi4r::cc_isopycnal_type() (iso_ + cc_isopycnal()'s variable: iso_depth_m, iso_temperature_ave, iso_salinity_ave_corr, iso_oxygen_ml_l_ave_sta_corr, iso_est_nitrate_sta_corr, iso_spiciness0), so its rows can never be mistaken for an obs series of the same quantity at a depth.

Usage

build_isopycnal(
  con,
  tbl = "isopycnal",
  sigma = NULL,
  variables = NULL,
  direction = "down",
  surface_max_m = NULL,
  min_n = NULL,
  batch = 20L,
  dataset_key = "calcofi_ctd-cast"
)

Arguments

con

DuckDB connection holding obs_ctd_full, sample and cruise (with month_median / date_median, add_cruise_median_date()).

tbl

output table (default "isopycnal").

sigma, variables, direction, surface_max_m, min_n

passed to calcofi4r::cc_isopycnal(); NULL keeps its default (the provider's list).

batch

cruises per call.

dataset_key

the CTD dataset whose casts are read.

Value

Invisibly, the row count of tbl. Columns: dataset_key, sample_key, cruise_key, site_key, grid_key, longitude, latitude, datetime, data_stage, year, month (the cruise's), sigma_theta, status, measurement_type, measurement_value.

Details

Asked for by Rasmus Swalethorp (2026-11-12/13): sigma-theta 24.0 to 27.0 by 0.2 plus 25.5 and 26.5, the shallowest crossing, depth / temperature / salinity / oxygen / estimated nitrate / spice on each surface, down casts, from the 1 m bins. Those are cc_isopycnal()'s defaults, which this function passes through unchanged unless told otherwise.

Every cast x surface keeps its iso_depth_m row whatever its status ("ok", "at_surface", "no_bracket", "not_reached", "no_data"; measurement_value NULL unless "ok"), so a surface that outcrops or is never reached stays distinguishable from a missing cast; a property's row is present only where the surface is "ok" and the property has a value there. The table carries no measurement_qual: every value is interpolated from bins the provider does not flag 8/9, after the sensor-pair rule.

build_climatology()(isopycnal_tbl = ) pools it into the surface baseline.
